knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A damp head lifts soil without flooding the floor, which would leave a slip hazard and excess product.
Starting with corners and edges, then moving toward the exit, keeps finished floor clear of footprints.
Soiled water puts the dirt back on the floor, so it should be replaced once it looks dirty.

practicalCriteria: Lifts mats and removes labels and gum before wet work.
Doses the solution to the label and fill mark, and wrings the head to damp.
Mops the corners and edges before working toward the exit, and changes the water when soiled.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. The practical sign-off is separate, observed by an assessor, and is not shown by a quiz result.
evidenceRequired: Observed practical sign-off on assessor sheet
Job record or photo of the finished area
stopWorkCriteria: Floor cleaner mixed above the label dose
Wet floor left without signs at an entrance
Cleaner used on a floor without checking it is suitable
